title: Al-Muqaddim, the Expediter
tomorrow: and when He puts something back, what then?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Muqtadir, the All-Powerful, and a dry leaf that tells a whole season. The line: all power. Today, power over the clock.

There's a tab you've had open for weeks. An email you starred and never answered. A call you'll make right after this one thing. Yesterday's question: is there a Name for that? There is, and it isn't a scolding. It's Al-Muqaddim, the Expediter, the one who brings forward. And the clearest teaching on it came with a hand on someone's shoulder.
screen: `THE TAB OPEN FOR WEEKS.` → `IS THERE A NAME FOR THAT?` → `A HAND ON A SHOULDER.`

segments.voice: Start with a prayer. In Sahih al-Bukhari, a du'a of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, ends by calling God the one who brings forward and the one who puts back. Two Names, side by side: today's, and tomorrow's. In this picture, what arrives first is not random. A chance, a person, a moment, an opening: God brings it forward. The Qur'an speaks of time the same way. Every people has its term, it says, and when the term comes, no one can put it back an hour or bring it forward. So what do you do with what's been brought forward? Here's the hand on the shoulder. Abdullah ibn Umar tells it in Bukhari: the Prophet took hold of his shoulder and said, be in this world as if you were a stranger, or a traveler on the road. A traveler doesn't redecorate the inn. And Ibn Umar turned it into advice of his own: when evening comes, don't wait for morning; when morning comes, don't wait for evening. Take from your health for your sickness, and from your life for your death. That's the line to tell a friend tonight. It isn't panic. It's noticing that what's in front of you today was brought forward on purpose, and that a road keeps moving.
screen: `THE ONE WHO BRINGS FORWARD.` · `NO ONE MOVES THE TERM.` · `A STRANGER, OR A TRAVELER.` · `DON'T WAIT FOR MORNING.` · then, large: `BROUGHT FORWARD.`

segments.voice: Bring the pushed-back thing to mind and shrink it to its first move: one sentence of the email, one box on the form, one text. If that move fits in a minute, make it now. Then let the rest of the sit hold the difference between done and someday.
screen: `THE PUSHED-BACK THING.` · `ITS FIRST MOVE.` · `DONE, NOT SOMEDAY.`

segments.voice: Al-Muqaddim. The Expediter: the one who brings forward whatever He wills, in His own order.
Here's the line: brought forward, to you, today, on purpose, by the one who keeps the clock. Peace till tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1545 COUNTS.` → `NAME 71 OF 99 · YEAR FIVE, 119 OF 365.` → `TOMORROW: AND WHEN HE PUTS SOMETHING BACK?`

howItsDone: Muslims who pray at night may use the Prophet's du'a that calls God the one who brings forward and the one who puts back; Ibn Umar's advice about evening and morning is often quoted in talks on using time well.

fork.setup: your little brother says he'll start his science project 'when he's in the mood.' it's due friday. what would Ibn Umar tell him?
options: start one small piece now: when evening comes, don't wait for morning.
wait for the mood; work that's forced never turns out well.
do the whole thing tonight in one push, then forget about it.
fork.reveal: Ibn Umar said: when evening comes, don't wait for morning. the point is what's in front of you now, not a heroic all-nighter.

original.note: Arabic: the Expediter, the one who brings forward. its partner Name is al-Mu'akhkhir.

trapdoor: what you thought: God speeds things up when you're in a hurry.
what it means: the one who brings forward whatever and whomever He wills, in His order.
what a scholar hears: the Prophet's du'a pairs al-Muqaddim with al-Mu'akhkhir (Bukhari); 7:34 speaks of a term no one can delay or bring forward.

chat.says: I GOT IN!!! but the aid letter's been sitting unopened for two days. i'm scared of the number
options: Open it today. It was brought forward to you; Ibn Umar said don't wait for evening.
Wait till you feel ready. Al-Muqaddim brings things forward in His time, not yours.

chat.meaning: Al-Muqaddim brings things forward, and Ibn Umar's advice was not to wait for the next evening. The letter is her next step.

Al-Muqaddim.meaning: the Expediter, who brings forward; a Name of Allah

Ibn Umar.meaning: Abdullah ibn Umar, a companion of the Prophet

du'a.meaning: personal prayer: asking Allah in your own words

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of the Prophet's sayings and deeds

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6398 (the Prophet's du'a: 'You are the one who brings forward and You are the one who puts back'); also Sahih Muslim 2719

Sahih al-Bukhari 6416 (be in this world as a stranger or a traveler; Ibn Umar: when evening comes, don't wait for morning)
